# TUI: the edit tool never shows a diff — the ± diff block kind has no producer

# Title

TUI: the `edit` tool never shows a diff — the `± diff` block kind has no producer

# Body

## Summary

An `edit` tool call renders as a head line and nothing else: no diff of what
changed, no line counts, no old/new text. The `diff` block kind — with its
documented `±` glyph, purple tint and per-line `+`/`-` colors — exists in the
codebase but **no code path produces it**: its only producer was deleted
(commit `78b654de`, #205) and nothing replaced it. This issue is both the
missing feature (an edit should show what it changed) and the dead grammar
(a kind that is declared, tinted, tested and documented, but unreachable).

Reported by the owner after noticing that moh edits files with no visible diff
in the transcript — confirmed by inspection before anything was changed.

## What the user sees today (verified)

**dev mode.** One `tool` block per call:

```
✓ edit  src/foo.ts
  edited src/foo.ts
```

- head: `edit` + `detailOf(args)` (`packages/tui/src/transcript.tsx:790-796`),
  and `detailOf` returns the first of `command|path|file|pattern|query|url` —
  so the path (`transcript.tsx:207-224`);
- body: the `tool_result` output, capped at 5 lines (15 when
  `filePreview: "always"`) — and the core's result is a single line,
  `edited <path>` (`packages/core/src/builtin-tools.ts:547`).

**vibe mode.** The whole call collapses to one flat line,
`edited a file · src/foo.ts` (`transcript.tsx:783`, `TOOL_ACTION.edit` at
`transcript.tsx:116`). That is the documented vibe behaviour (style guide §2:
tool activity collapses to one plain-language line) — the diff belongs to
`dev`.

**The permission prompt is just as blind.** For any path-carrying tool the
modal shows only `path: <path>` (`packages/tui/src/permission-gate.ts:82-88`);
the only way to see the pending change before answering is `e`
(`PermissionModal.tsx:110-123`), which opens the file in `$EDITOR`.

**`filePreview` does not help.** It only caps preview/output rows
(`transcript.tsx:773`, `804-806`); a numbered preview block (`kind: "code"`) is
emitted for `read` only. `write` shows just `wrote N bytes to <path>`
(`builtin-tools.ts:523`).

**The only diff a user ever sees** is one the model writes itself in a
```diff fence: that goes through the markdown renderer, and highlight.js does
have `diff` (`supportsLanguage("diff") === true`, verified against the bundled
cli-highlight). It is the model's text, not the change actually applied.

## Evidence

### 1. The `diff` kind is declared, painted, tested — and never built

```
grep -rn 'kind: "diff"' packages/   # the whole tree
```

returns only declarations and readers, never a producer:

- `packages/tui/src/transcript.tsx:17` — the union member
  (`BlockKind = … | "code" | "diff" | …`);
- `transcript.tsx:1480` — purple tint (`code`/`diff` share it);
- `transcript.tsx:1617` — the per-line colors, the whole `diff` treatment:
  `startsWith("+") → theme.ok`, `startsWith("-") → theme.err`, else `dim`;
- `packages/tui/src/ThemeStudioModal.tsx:173` — the studio's swatch;
- `packages/tui/test/block-surfaces.test.tsx:109` — `diff` is in the tinted
  set asserted row-by-row for the #1305 continuous-surface work.

Nothing else. There is no `blocks.push({ … kind: "diff" … })` anywhere in the
repository.

### 2. It had exactly one producer, and #205 deleted it

```bash
git log --oneline -S'"diff"' -- packages/tui/src/transcript.tsx
# 78b654de Render one assistant reply as one continuous Markdown output (#205)
# 28dec7ed feat(tui): implement native scrollback session layout (#183)
```

`28dec7ed` (#183) introduced the kind with a markdown-fence arm:

```ts
blocks.push({ key: `${key}-code-${match.index}`, kind: lang === "diff" ? "diff" : "code", glyph: lang === "diff" ? "±" : "⌨", type: lang === "diff" ? "diff" : "code", detail: lang || undefined, lines: … });
```

`78b654de` (#205, "one assistant reply as one continuous Markdown output")
removed that arm when replies moved to the markdown renderer, and both the
fence-`code` and the fence-`diff` producers went with it. The `code` kind was
later re-populated by the `read` preview block; **`diff` was not**, and has
been unreachable since 2026-08-25.

### 3. The documented grammar still promises it

`docs/tui-style-guide.md:32` (§2 transcript block grammar):

> `⌨ code` / `± diff`: code and diffs, purple tint; additions use `ok`,
> removals use `err`.

and line 103 repeats it for the palette audit ("`err` … is used for failures,
errors, **diff removals** and negative edit counts"). The `#1305` work item
lists `diff` among the tinted kinds that must paint every cell. So the
grammar, the palette contract and the surface tests all describe a block that
cannot appear — the mismatch is the second half of this issue.

### 4. The diff is derivable, at projection time, without touching the log

`edit`'s arguments carry both sides of the change
(`builtin-tools.ts:527-531`: `path`, `oldText`, `newText`) and they are
persisted in the `tool_call` event — which is why every other consumer
(consent rules, the Jev gate's `diff`, session analysis) can already see them.
`projectTranscript` has the event in hand when it builds the block, so a
unified diff can be computed where the block is built, exactly as `read`'s
preview block is appended as a second block beside the tool block
(`transcript.tsx:804-807`).

## The owner's observation, restated as acceptance criteria

1. A **successful `edit`** call in **dev mode** shows what changed: a diff
   block carrying the removed and added lines, with the existing `ok`/`err`
   per-line coloring and the `±` glyph (or a deliberately re-decided shape).
2. The diff is **derived from the logged event** (args + result), not from a
   fresh read of the file — a resumed session, a fork and a replay must show
   the same block, byte for byte.
3. It is **bounded** like every other block (no unbounded growth in the
   scrollback): a cap with a visible indication when it truncates.
4. A **failed** `edit` (oldText not found / not unique) keeps rendering as the
   error block it is today — no invented diff for a change that did not happen.
5. **vibe mode is unchanged**: one plain-language line, per style guide §2.
6. No event is added and the log is never rewritten: this is a projection
   change only.
7. The block paints like the other tinted surfaces (#1305 contract), and the
   existing `block-surfaces` / `transcript` tests keep passing.

## Open decisions for the owner

Every decision carries a **marked default** — an agent may take the default and
ship, and the owner can steer in a comment at any time.

a. **Which tools get it.** `edit` only, or also `write` (an all-additions diff
   for a new file) and any future multi-edit/patch tool?
   **Default: `edit` only** — `write` shows a byte count today and a
   whole-file diff is a different review shape; extend later if wanted.
b. **Shape and budget.** Headline with `+N/−M` counts? How many context lines
   around the change, and what is the cap once a diff is long?
   **Default: head `± edit <path> · +N −M`, 3 context lines, cap 40 body rows
   with a trailing `… N more lines` row** (bounded like every other block).
c. **`filePreview` interaction.** Always show (a change to the file is not a
   "preview"), or honour `always`/`on-demand`/`none` like the `read` preview?
   **Default: always show the diff for `edit`** — it is the record of a change
   that happened, not a preview of a file the user has not read.
d. **The permission prompt.** Show the pending change in the modal too (today:
   `path:` only), or keep the modal as-is and leave the diff to the transcript?
   **Default: leave the modal as-is in this ticket** and file the modal case
   as its own ticket (related defect 2) — it is a different surface with its own
   copy and keymap.
e. **Keep the `diff` kind** (revive it, as this issue assumes) **or drop it**
   and reuse `code`? **Default: revive it** — the style guide, the palette audit
   and `block-surfaces.test.tsx` already encode it; dropping it means editing
   three documents for no gain.

## Constraints any implementation must respect

- **Determinism (#194).** A settled block must never mutate after Static
  promotion: the diff is computed once, from immutable events, and the block
  key follows the existing log-index convention.
- **Redaction (ADR-0058).** The log's `tool_call` args are already redacted at
  the write seam. Derive the diff from those args and never read the file from
  disk at projection time — a disk read would show un-redacted bytes for a
  resumed session and break replay purity.
- **Log fidelity.** Projection may group and pair events but must not discard
  an event type or rewrite the log (style guide §2; CONTEXT.md "Event log").
- **Width.** Body rows go through `Row`, which already paints full width for
  tinted kinds (#1305); a diff row must not become a `width - 1` hole. Note
  ink forbids a `<Box>` inside a `<Text>` — the #1305 bench hit this and the
  fix is in the same file.
- **Tests.** ADR-0057: the in-process fake terminal is the behavioural gate
  (`packages/tui/test/`, `renderOnFakeTty`); a `tui-pty` test is only for a
  process-boundary claim. Widened lines (a `+`/`-` body that wraps) are a
  cell-level concern — assert raw bytes where a string assertion cannot see a
  missing escape cell.
- **Docs.** No `docs/manual/` page documents block surfaces (verified: the
  manual covers keys, commands and config) — so no manual page needs the
  light-alignment update unless the decision in (a)-(d) changes a documented
  door. `docs/tui-style-guide.md` §2/§3 is the page that must end up true, and
  it is the one to update if the `diff` grammar changes.

## Related defects found while investigating (separate tickets — not this one)

1. **`ctrl+d` "toggle tool-call detail" is advertised and does nothing.**
   `packages/tui/src/CommandsPanel.tsx:24` lists it for the Chat area and the
   generated mirror `docs/manual/commands-and-keys.md:19` repeats it, but no
   handler exists in `App.tsx` or `Chat.tsx`: the `key.ctrl && input === "d"`
   handler was **removed when the chat moved to native scrollback**
   (`28dec7ed`, #183) — the key survived only in the key list. In `Home.tsx:326`
   the same chord means "delete the selected session", so the shared panel
   shows two different meanings and only one of them is wired.
2. **The `edit` permission prompt cannot show the change** (see above):
   `path:` only, for a tool whose whole purpose is a content change.
3. **The `±` glyph is referenced by no producer** (`28dec7ed`'s arm was the
   only user); if the kind is revived, the glyph returns with it; if it is
   dropped, the section of the style guide that names it goes too.

## Reproduction

1. Run the TUI in dev mode and have the agent edit any file — the `edit` block
   shows the head and `edited <path>`, and nothing else.
2. Static check: `grep -rn 'kind: "diff"' packages/` — five hits, none of them
   a producer. `git log --oneline -S'"diff"' -- packages/tui/src/transcript.tsx`
   names the commit that removed the only one.
3. Unit-level: `projectTranscript` with an `edit` `tool_call` + `tool_result`
   fixture yields exactly one `kind: "tool"` block (see
   `packages/tui/test/transcript.test.tsx` for the existing projection tests).

## Suggested work item outline

1. **The projection**: when `event.name === "edit"` and the result is `ok`,
   append a `kind: "diff"` block beside the tool block (same pattern as the
   `read` preview block), built from `oldText`/`newText` with a bounded unified
   diff. Keep the tool block as it is (it is the record of the call).
2. **The renderer**: confirm `Row`/tint/`±`/per-line colors behave for the
   revived kind (they should, untouched) and that a long or wrapped diff row
   paints every cell.
3. **Tests**: a projection test (block emitted, bounded, failed edit → none), a
   fake-terminal test for the painted rows, and the byte-level edge check for a
   wrapped `+`/`-` row.
4. **Docs**: only if a decision above changes the grammar —
   `docs/tui-style-guide.md` §2, and a `CHANGELOG.md` entry. Consider fixing
   related defect (1) under a separate ticket so this one stays reviewable.

Implement this issue.

# Notes modal: cursor-based editing, word wrap, and inject-note-into-composer

- moh version: 0.56.0
- OS: macOS (darwin/arm64)
- Install: source

## Problem

The notes modal (`packages/tui/src/NotesModal.tsx`) has three editing limitations:

1. The note editor is append-only: typed characters and newlines are concatenated
   at the end and backspace always removes the last character. There is no visible
   cursor and no way to move within the text to edit an arbitrary position.
2. Long lines are rendered with `wrap="truncate"`, so text is cut at the dialog
   border instead of wrapping. Typing past the border is effectively invisible.
3. There is no way to move a note's content into the chat composer; the user must
   copy it manually.

## Proposed solution

1. **Cursor-based editor** — track a cursor offset within the note text, render it
   visibly, and support left/right/up/down movement (plus home/end as convenient)
   so any position is editable. Backspace/delete act at the cursor.
2. **Word wrap** — render editor lines with wrapping (not truncation) so text flows
   to the next line at the dialog border; the visible-row budget must account for
   wrapped visual rows, not just logical `\n` lines.
3. **Inject into composer** — with a note selected in the list, a key (e.g. `i`)
   closes the modal and prefills the chat composer with the note's text. The seam
   already exists: the composer `prefill` prop (`Input.tsx`) drives `replaceText`,
   as used by claimed-issue prefill.

## Notes

- Keep the existing key conventions (ctrl+s save, esc confirm/discard, ctrl+z restore).
- Word wrap changes the editing viewport math; the windowing budget should be
  computed on visual rows to keep scrolling correct.

Implement this issue.

# TUI: single ctrl+c clears the composer when it has text

- moh version: 0.50.3
- OS: Darwin/arm64
- Install: binary

## Problem
There is no way to clear the composer in one gesture: a draft (often
multi-line, pasted, or a long recalled history entry) must be deleted
manually. Today a single ctrl+c only arms the exit toast ("press ctrl+c
again to exit") and does nothing to the text.

## Proposed solution
When the chat composer is focused, enabled, and non-empty, a single
ctrl+c clears the whole text area; when it is empty, ctrl+c keeps the
current double-press exit semantics.

Details:
- The clear must go through the editor's undo snapshot (`record()`), so
  ctrl+z restores the cleared draft.
- The clear must reset the exit arm (`exitArmRef`), so the next ctrl+c
  starts a fresh sequence: no accidental exit from clear → clear → exit.
- Scope: the chat composer only — not over overlays/modals, not while
  the composer is blocked, and not the Home search input (follow-up if
  wanted).
- Implementation seam: the ctrl+c handler lives in App's useInput while
  the text state lives in MultilineInput — expose a shared ref
  (hasText + imperative clear()) or let the composer consume the key
  with App deferring.
- Docs: the manual page documenting exit (double ctrl+c) is updated in
  the same PR (light-alignment rule).

Alternative considered: esc-to-clear (Claude Code style) — rejected
because esc is already the double-press turn interrupt ("esc stop").

Tests: extend packages/tui/test/exit-keys.test.tsx (text + ctrl+c →
cleared, undo restores; ctrl+c after clear arms, does not exit; lone
ctrl+c on empty composer unchanged).

Implement this issue.

# Jev transcript noise: one valueless guardrail line per bash call

## Summary

Every judged `bash` call appends a `jev_judgment` event, and the transcript renders each one as its own `◈ jev · guardrail` chrome block. A tool-heavy turn therefore produces dozens of identical, information-free lines, and the line cannot be made informative as things stand: the record does not carry the verdict.

## Evidence (real session logs)

- Session `20260920T072807329Z` turn 1: 65 `bash` calls, 65 guardrail judgments, 50 of them rendered as `◈ jev · guardrail` before the per-turn cap dropped the rest.
- Across the local session history: 75 guardrail judgments in one session, every one of them rendering the bare string `jev · guardrail`.
- The record's payload keys are `useCase`, `callId`, `tool`, `lethalOnly`, `state`, `answers`, `model`, `latencyMs`, `usage` — **no verdict**. The guardrail's decision (`pass` / `ask` / `deny`) is computed after the record is built, so the transcript renderer has nothing to phrase.

## Current behavior

- One `◈ jev · guardrail` block per judged `bash` call, in both transcript modes.
- The line is identical for a pass, an ask and a deny. A pass changed nothing and is pure noise; an ask and a deny are already visible where they matter (the permission prompt and the vetoed `tool_result`).
- The record is also incomplete as an audit artifact: it says what was measured but never what was decided.

## Desired behavior

1. The guardrail judgment record carries its outcome (`decision`: `pass` / `ask` / `deny`, and for an ask the key probability it was based on), so a `jev_judgment` is a complete record of the judgment.
2. The transcript shows **only the notable outcomes**: an `ask` and a `deny` get a line (e.g. `jev · guardrail · ask (destructive 0.42)`); a `pass` gets none — nothing happened to the user.
3. The event log stays complete and unsampled: every judgment is still recorded, only the projection changes.
4. This issue fixes **which single judgments earn a line**; how many lines one turn may produce is *Jev guardrail lines repeat once per bash call*'s job. Implementing this issue alone may leave several notable outcomes in one turn — that is expected, not a gap.

## Key interfaces

- The guardrail judge's judgment record: gains the verdict it already computes, plus the key probability on an ask.
- The transcript projection's extension-event phraser (`extensionEventLine`) and its silent-band helper (`isSilentInjection`, today injection-only): the guardrail needs the same treatment — a predicate that says "this judgment earns no line".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A guardrail `pass` produces no transcript block; an `ask` and a `deny` each produce one, carrying the deciding probability.
- [ ] The session log still contains one `jev_judgment` per judged call, and each now names its verdict.
- [ ] Resume/replay of an old session renders identically to the live turn.
- [ ] Tests: a projection test per verdict (pass renders nothing, ask and deny render one line each) and a judge test asserting the verdict is in the record.

## Docs

The Jev manual page is generated: its **source** lives in the core's bundled
manual assets, and `docs/manual/` is a build-time mirror (ADR-0013). Edit the
source and regenerate the mirror — never edit the mirror directly. The page describes the transcript lines a judgment leaves, so it changes in the same PR (light alignment).

## Out of scope

- The per-turn event cap (*Jev per-turn event cap silently disarms the extension mid-turn*) — this issue does not change it, though it removes most of the volume that trips it.
- Vibe-mode filtering (*Jev in vibe mode: the whole audit trail still renders*).
- Changing the guardrail's thresholds, caching or decision rule.

## Filed together

Six issues from one session's evidence. Each stands alone and can be implemented
on its own; the only ordering constraint is that the per-turn collapse reads the
verdict that the first issue adds to the guardrail's record.

- Jev guardrail lines repeat once per bash call; the transcript needs one line per turn
- Jev in vibe mode: the whole audit trail still renders
- Jev per-turn event cap silently disarms the extension mid-turn
- Jev routing mismatch notice renders as a bare line
- Jev manual promises a record per cache hit; the code records none

Implement this issue.

# Browser SSRF guard: loopback-only default + allowedHosts

## Parent

#769 (feature), ADR-0029. Spec: docs/spec/browser-tool.md (local-only).

## What to build

The navigation layer enforces the network posture: loopback allowed by default (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]` — the dev-debugging use case), all other private ranges and link-local blocked (`169.254.x` cloud metadata, `192.168.x`, `10.x`, `172.16–31.x`) — the prompt-injection SSRF defense. Same DNS-verification philosophy as fetch (#697/SEC-05) applied at the navigation layer, with redirect hops re-checked. `browser.allowedHosts` (exact-host config list) is the only escape hatch; env-var overrides like `MOH_FETCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE` do not apply to the browser.

Blocked navigations fail with a clear, model-readable reason naming the policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `navigate http://localhost:PORT` works by default (loopback dev use case).
- [ ] `navigate` to `169.254.169.254`, `192.168.1.1`, `10.0.0.1`, `172.16.x` blocked with a clear reason.
- [ ] A redirect that bounces a public URL into a private address is caught (per-hop re-check).
- [ ] `browser.allowedHosts: ["host.example"]` permits exactly that host; no wildcard subdomain matching.
- [ ] Blocked pages cannot be reached by the model retrying with different wording (the guard is at the navigation layer, not prompt-level).

## Blocked by

- #1 Browser tool skeleton (navigation must exist).

Implement this issue.

# Project identity: canonical remote slug

## What to build

A project's identity is derived from its git `origin` remote instead of a locally-generated UUID, so two clones of the same repository on different machines share one project identity (sessions, memory, handoff all land in the same `~/.moh/projects/<slug>` directory).

Rule: when `origin` exists, the identity comes from its canonical form `host/owner/repo` (case-insensitive; protocol, trailing `.git`, and embedded credentials ignored — `git@github.com:owner/repo.git`, `https://github.com/owner/repo.git` and `ssh://git@github.com/owner/repo.git` must all yield the same slug). When there is no `origin` (or no git at all), the existing UUID-derived identity stays as fallback, unchanged.

This is the root fix for the failed handoff discovery on a fresh clone: today a cold directory generates a new random UUID, so the deterministic gist tag `moh:handoff:<slug>:<user>` never matches the one published by the other machine.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A project with `origin` derives its slug from the canonical `host/owner/repo` form.
- [ ] SSH, HTTPS, and ssh-URL spellings of the same remote all resolve to the same slug (test covers all three plus credential-bearing URLs).
- [ ] Case differences in host/owner/repo do not change the slug.
- [ ] A project without `origin` keeps the current UUID-derived slug (no behavior change for non-git projects).
- [ ] The legacy path-derived slug fallback is preserved for unreadable-identity situations, as today.
- [ ] The resolver is a core-level seam; existing callers of the project-identity resolution get the new behavior without interface changes.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

Implement this issue.

# spawn: register the tool by default (discoverability) + pre-validate child provider refs

## Summary

Two related follow-ups from the live spawn analysis (#328 session, 2026-08-30). Cumulative issue per owner decision.

### Part 1 — Discoverability: `spawn` should be registered by default (A1)

Today the `spawn` tool is registered only when `config.subagents` is set (`packages/core/src/session/session.ts` ~L145), and `from-config.ts` (~L203) sets it only when moh.json has an `agents` section. But the built-in presets (`research`: read/glob/grep/fetch; `implement`: read/write/edit/bash/glob/grep) are designed to work with **zero configuration** — the gate on the mere existence of the `agents` key makes subagents a hidden feature no user discovers (observed live: owner's sessions never had the tool until `"agents": {}` was added manually).

**Desired:** register `spawn` by default (zero-config); the moh.json `agents` section remains the way to *override* presets/provider/maxConcurrency. Safety invariants already hold and must keep holding: depth 1 by construction (children are created without the subagents option), children inherit the parent's permissions (never more permissively), MCP tools never inherited, semaphore-bounded concurrency.

### Part 2 — Pre-validate child provider refs before creating the child (B2)

`spawnInputSchema` accepts inline `provider`/`model`. Live observation: the model hallucinated refs on 3 consecutive calls; each failed at `resolveProviderRef` **after** child-session setup began (session store creation etc.), returning a structured error and wasting turns before the model learned. Note: there is NO silent mock fallback in the child path — `resolveProviderRef` throws on unknown refs and the catch in `#spawn` returns `{status:"error"}`; the mock seen live was the parent session's provider, not a child fallback.

**Desired:** resolve `spec.provider`/`spec.model` against the registry + configured endpoints **before** any child setup (store, session); on failure return an immediate, didactic error result (e.g. `unknown provider "X" — use a preset or omit provider/model`) without side effects. Inline provider/model remain allowed (flexibility to delegate to a cheaper model is kept — owner decision B2 over schema-restrictive B1).

**Bonus (B3, cheap):** strengthen the spawn tool description to recommend `preset` + `task` only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh session in a project with no `agents` key exposes the `spawn` tool with the built-in presets
- [ ] `agents: {}` in moh.json behaves identically to today's post-manual-fix behavior
- [ ] `agents` overrides (presets/provider/maxConcurrency) still work; depth-1, permission-inheritance, no-MCP-inheritance invariants pinned by tests
- [ ] A spawn call with an invalid inline `provider`/`model` ref fails fast with a clear error, no child store/session side effects
- [ ] A spawn call with a valid ref proceeds exactly as today

## Out of scope

- Schema-level rejection of inline provider/model (B1 — rejected)
- Multi-level subagents, subagent UI changes

Implement this issue.

Users adding known OpenAI-compat providers (or local runtimes) must hunt for the right endpoint themselves. Show a curated, selectable list of known endpoints that prefills the field. # Turn dies at max-iterations cap (50) mid-implementation — agent should deliver or checkpoint, not lose the turn

## What happened

Live session `20260825T144314460Z-76b0423c` (develop @ 9d47261): a single direct implementation request (collapse the `/ask-moh` envelope in the transcript) ran until the iteration cap:

```
error: max_iterations — iteration cap of 50 reached
```

The turn was **lost**: 51 model calls, 64 tool calls, 42 permission grants — real work happened (core/index.ts, prompt-composer.ts, transcript.tsx, commands.ts edits + typechecks) — but the user got only the cap message. The user had to type "continua" to restart, with the agent re-orienting from the event log.

## Why this matters

- Work-in-progress at the cap is not summarized or checkpointed: the user gets no "here's where I got to" — just a terminal error.
- 50 iterations of a well-behaved implementation loop is plausibly not enough for multi-file changes (explore → edit → typecheck → test cycles burn iterations fast).
- Related friction in the same turn: 42 manual permission grants (every tool ask) made the session slow; `always`/auto-accept mitigates per-user but the iteration economy is the structural issue.

## Ideas (to be triaged)

1. **Raise or make configurable the cap** (e.g. `maxIterations` in moh.json, default higher than 50 for interactive sessions).
2. **Graceful cap handling**: when the cap hits, have the core inject a final model call with a "wrap up now" instruction (budget-aware completion) instead of a bare error — the agent summarizes state and next steps into the transcript.
3. **Turn checkpointing**: persist enough turn state that `continua` (or an automatic retry) resumes without re-exploration.

## Evidence

- Log tail before the error: last calls were test-file reads (`mock-provider.ts`, `session.test.ts`) — the agent was mid-verification, not looping.
